findings.title: No Documented API Interface — CGI Returns HTML
findings.description: The application exposes a CGI endpoint at /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi via Apache HTTP that accepts GET requests with query parameters (sku, qty). The response is Content-Type: text/html — raw HTML markup, not a structured machine-readable format. No REST API, GraphQL schema, or AsyncAPI interface exists. Agent integration requires HTML parsing.
findings.gap: No machine-readable API interface exists. The only integration surface outputs unstructured HTML.
findings.recommendation: Add a JSON response mode — accept an Accept: application/json header or format=json query parameter. Implement proper HTTP status codes for error conditions.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add JSON response mode with format=json query parameter
blocker_remediation.target_state: Documented REST endpoint returning structured JSON with proper HTTP status codes

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application has zero authentication. No OAuth2 client credentials, no API key validation, no mTLS, no authentication middleware. Any network-reachable client can call the endpoint without identity attribution. The Kubernetes deployment defines no authentication mechanism.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication exists. Agent calls cannot be attributed to a specific principal.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an API Gateway in front of the service that requires API key or OAuth2 client credentials for access. Configure principal attribution in access logs.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Deploy API Gateway with API key authentication
blocker_remediation.target_state: All requests authenticated via machine identity with identity recorded in audit logs

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: No authorization model exists. The application has no concept of permissions, roles, or access scopes. Every caller has identical unrestricted access to all pricing data.
findings.gap: No mechanism to create scoped permissions for different callers.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway usage plans with per-key scoping to differentiate agent access levels.

compensating_controls: Deploy Kubernetes NetworkPolicy restricting pod access
API Gateway with usage plans and API keys

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No authorization enforcement exists at any level. The application cannot distinguish between callers with different permission levels.
findings.gap: No action-level authorization. Cannot restrict agents to specific product categories.
findings.recommendation: Add role-based access control at the gateway layer with method-level restrictions.

compensating_controls: API Gateway resource policies restricting to GET only

findings.title: No Input Validation — Buffer Overflow and XSS
findings.description: No input validation exists. The parse_query function uses strcpy to copy attacker-controlled query string data into fixed-size buffers without length checks (buffer overflow). The SKU parameter is reflected directly into HTML output without escaping (XSS). No bounds checking on qty parameter.
findings.gap: Zero input validation at API boundary. Active security vulnerabilities (buffer overflow, XSS).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite input parsing with bounded string operations (strncpy, length validation). Add SKU format validation. Escape HTML output. Return structured errors for invalid inputs.

compensating_controls: Deploy AWS WAF to filter malicious inputs
Limit query string length at Apache/ingress level

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No API versioning, no schema documentation, no breaking change detection. The CGI endpoint has no version prefix, no changelog, and no contract tests.
findings.gap: No schema versioning or API contracts. Agent tool bindings have no stability guarantees.
findings.recommendation: Create an OpenAPI specification. Add URL versioning (/v1/pricing). Implement contract tests in CI.

compensating_controls: Pin agent tool definitions to current known behavior
Document current interface in OpenAPI spec

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or Smithy model found. Interface documentation limited to README describing CGI query parameters informally. Dev-library-application override applied.
findings.gap: No machine-readable specification for agent tool generation.
findings.recommendation: Generate OpenAPI spec when JSON response mode is implemented.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No structured error responses. Unknown SKUs return HTML with $0.00 prices — no HTTP error status, no error code, no retryable indicator. Dev-library-application override applied.
findings.gap: No error codes or machine-readable error format.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON error responses with codes and retry categories.

findings.title: Response Format is HTML
findings.description: Response format is Content-Type: text/html. Raw HTML markup with embedded pricing data. Not machine-readable without HTML parsing.
findings.gap: HTML response requires parsing for agent consumption.
findings.recommendation: Add JSON response support as part of API modernization.

findings.title: No Rate Limit Documentation or Headers
findings.description: No rate limit documentation or headers. No API Gateway usage plan, no WAF rate rules, no rate limiting middleware.
findings.gap: Agents have no signal to self-throttle.
findings.recommendation: Document rate limits and add standard headers when deploying API Gateway.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation
findings.description: No identity propagation. No JWT middleware, no token exchange, no user context headers. Stateless utility serving reference data — identity propagation is not operationally critical.
findings.gap: No identity context awareness.
findings.recommendation: Add identity propagation at gateway layer if integrated into user-context workflows.

findings.title: No Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging. System has no auth surface and no write operations — audit logging is a consumer responsibility until authentication is added.
findings.gap: No audit trail for requests.
findings.recommendation: Add audit logging when authentication is deployed.

ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Surface calibration applied — system has no authentication surface and no write operations. Audit logging responsibility belongs to the consuming application or gateway layer.

items.summary: Resolve the two BLOCKERs (no API interface, no authentication) and address critical RISK-SAFETY findings (no scoped permissions, no action-level auth). Deploy API Gateway with authentication, scoped access, and JSON response support.
Fix input validation vulnerabilities (buffer overflow, XSS) and establish API contract stability through versioning and schema documentation.
Add machine-readable API specification, structured error responses, observability instrumentation, and staging environment.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy API Gateway with authentication and JSON response support
recommended_actions.rationale: Resolves both BLOCKERs and RISK-SAFETY findings simultaneously. An API Gateway provides machine identity (AUTH-Q1), scoped permissions (AUTH-Q2), action-level auth (AUTH-Q3), and rate limiting (STATE-Q5). Combined with adding JSON response support, this unblocks agent integration.

recommended_actions.action: Fix input validation and security vulnerabilities
recommended_actions.rationale: Buffer overflow and XSS vulnerabilities are active security risks. Rewrite input parsing with bounds checking and output escaping.

recommended_actions.action: Create OpenAPI specification and implement versioning
recommended_actions.rationale: Enables automated agent tool generation and provides contract stability for agent bindings.
